Red is meat and tomato, Grey is fertilisers and Black is petroleum, so a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii (A).

All four pairs are correct: the Blue Revolution (fisheries) is linked with Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan, Pink (meat processing, prawn, onion) with Durgesh Patel, Red (meat and tomato) with Vishal Tewari, and Golden (horticulture and honey) with Nirpakh Tutej. Hence a, b, c and d (D).

SMAM (2014-15 to 2025-26) set up 27,563 custom hiring centres nationally, and Andhra Pradesh had 239 CHCs in 2025-26 (75 of them with Kisan Drones). Some notes give a lower national count of 25,689; 25,260 is the number of farm machinery banks and 529 is AP's drone figure.

All three are correct. The Soil Health Card scheme belongs to 2014-15 and was launched in 2015; cards are issued free every two years; and they are associated with an 8-10% cut in fertiliser use and a 5-6% rise in yields. Hence D.

All four are correct: NMSA is one of the 8 NAPCC missions, focuses on climate-resilient rainfed farming, became a sub-mission of Krishonnati from 2018-19, and has been under PM-RKVY since 2022-23. Hence D.

Neem-based pesticides are plant-derived bio-pesticides, the safer alternative to chemical pesticides that the draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 and IPM seek to promote. They are not synthetic, fumigant or organophosphate chemicals.

The call for a Second Green Revolution was made by PM Manmohan Singh (APPSC 2025). M.S. Swaminathan coined the related term 'Evergreen Revolution', and Norman Borlaug is linked with the original Mexican dwarf wheats.

'Tilhan' means oilseeds, so the Tilhan Mission (Feb 2020, PYQ) relates to oilseed production, in the line of the Technology Mission on Oilseeds and NMEO. Pulses have a separate mission (Aatmanirbharta in Pulses) and millets come under INSIMP.
Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by Subhash Palekar. Rythu Sadhikara Samstha only runs AP's natural-farming programme (APCNF), and APEDA handles NPOP organic certification.
India ranks second in the world in silk, along with wheat, sugarcane, fruits, vegetables, eggs and cotton. India is first in milk, pulses, spices, millets and jute.
